summary: Emit canonical agent identities in mission presentation while preserving historical writer spelling

replay.detail: Historical rows remain unchanged; presentation canonicalizes legacy slash-qualified agent identities on read. Re-parsing stored declarations preserves historical host-relative qualification and malformed assignee normalization rather than rejecting them.

schema.detail: The strict client AgentId schema and database schema are unchanged.

rules.detail: Work reads, renewal polling and presentation compare canonical identities. All mutations preserve main's literal actor matching, including ownership admission, eligibility, capacity, queue admission, carried-claim successor selection, output authority and ancestor lease extension. An unexpired legacy-owned lease refuses a differently spelled actor with work-already-claimed when the literal eligibility selector admits that actor, without changing claim state, publishing a mutation or extending the operational lease. Renewal, release and completion retain the same fence; successful child mutations extend only literally owned ancestor leases. Work read filters retain default-agent qualification for bare names, including published lists and explicit ready-work queue ordering. Declaration, run-start and successful work ownership writes retain main's spelling during expansion; local work actions refuse malformed or unprefixed claimants that old validators reject, with a typed error directing callers to the canonical spelling.

compatibility.detail: Expand phase only: read both actor spellings and preserve the previous writer spelling, with no feature gate or capability advertisement. LIVE-MIGRATION BRIDGE arn:lmig:fractal:2026-11-07-agent-actor-ownership: a later spelling switch and stored-row migration require a durable one-way fleet fence. Once raw legacy-signed ownership facts exist, the historical reader floor must prohibit old readers that cannot admit those facts; a reversible capability check cannot establish that floor.

downtime.detail: No downtime or stored-row migration is required for this read-compatible expansion.

recovery.detail: Lease fencing remains unchanged. Signed legacy work ownership can arrive before its target row during cold import; projection checks canonical eligibility and records a defect without taking the lease if the target selector does not match.
